definitions.explanation: Fruit whose moisture has been removed through sun-drying, hot-air drying, or freeze-drying. The formal, written-Japanese equivalent of the more common everyday term ドライフルーツ.

examples.japanese: {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}を{食|た}べる。
この{店|みせ}では{様々|さまざま}な{乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}を{扱|あつか}っている。
examples.english: This shop carries various kinds of dried fruit.

examples.japanese: {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}は{栄養|えいよう}{価|か}が{高|たか}く、{保存|ほぞん}にも{向|む}いている。
examples.english: Dried fruit is high in nutritional value and keeps well.

notes:
Compound of {乾燥|かんそう} ('drying; dehydration') and {果実|かじつ} ('fruit'). A formal term for dried fruit, appearing mainly in labeling, ingredient lists, nutritional writing, and food-industry texts.

USAGE:
- In everyday conversation, Japanese speakers overwhelmingly prefer the loanword ドライフルーツ.
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ} appears on packaging ingredient lists, customs documents, food-safety regulations, and nutritional articles.
- Common examples of dried fruit: レーズン (raisins), プルーン (prunes), ドライマンゴー (dried mango), {干|ほ}し{柿|がき} (dried persimmon), {干|ほ}しブドウ (dried grapes/raisins).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}を{食|た}べる: to eat dried fruit
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}を{加|くわ}える: to add dried fruit (to a recipe)
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}{入|い}り: containing dried fruit
- {乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}ミックス: dried fruit mix

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ドライフルーツ: dried fruit — everyday, casual loanword; the default term in speech and most food packaging.
- {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}: dried fruit — native Japanese expression using the verb {干|ほ}す ('to dry in the sun'); somewhat old-fashioned.
- {干|ほ}し{柿|がき}: dried persimmon — a specific traditional Japanese example.
- {果実|かじつ}: fruit — the formal counterpart of {果物|くだもの}.
